history.p: After having spent some years in Sønderborg, where Scheibe established a music school for children, the family decided to return to Copenhagen in 1761 due to the political tensions caused by the Seven Years' War (1756–1763). Scheibe advertised in the newspaper that he intended to provide lessons in accompaniment and composition and he participated in the discussions concerning emotions, text and music among the German intellectuals. Heinrich Wilhelm von Gerstenberg, who was an able keyboard player, was famous for his musical gatherings which included among others Friedrich Gottlieb Klopstock; it seems likely that Scheibe participated in these gatherings. At some point during the middle of the 1760s, Scheibe was living in the house of Gerstenberg and they worked closely together on the present cantata, 'Adriadne auf Naxos', discussing textual as well as musical issues.The plan was that Scheibe should also compose music to another of Gerstenberg’s texts, ‘Clarissa’; however, that came to nothing as Scheibe at that time had moved from Gerstenberg’s house. The present cantata is for harpsichord and vocal soloists though Scheibe remarks that a version for orchestra would support and express the text much better. An extensive review appeared in Bibliothek der schönen Wissenschaften (1765) edited by Christian Felix Weiße. The review is positive and includes excerpts from the cantata. Another thorough review appeared in Allgemeine deutsche Bibliothek (1769) by the composer Johann Friedrich Agricola. He also deals with instrumentation, the setting of the text and includes analyses and music examples. And in the obituary published in Berlinisches Litterarisches Wochenblatt, it is mentioned that the present cantata is one of Scheibe's best musical works. See also introduction to SchW B2:Coll.001.

incipText.p: O du, wie kann ich dich zu zärtlich lieben?
Zu weit entfernt das Meer den Frevler schon!
Kannst du, mein Herz, unter diesem stechenden Schmerz
Weh mir! warum mußt ich ihn sehn?
Daß er der Fluch der Menschheit werde!
